dosageRegimens.notes: OTC strength. May be taken up to 30 minutes before a meal expected to cause symptoms.

Prescription dosing, at bedtime. The alternative divided-dose regimen is 300 mg four times daily (1200 mg/day) or 400 mg twice daily; those are different regimens with different ceilings and should not share this one.

interactions.suggestedAction: Expect a normal amount of caffeine to feel stronger and last considerably longer. Cut the dose, especially in the afternoon.
interactions.note: CYP1A2 inhibition. Caffeine half-life rises by roughly 50-70%, so an evening cut-off that normally works stops working.

interactions.suggestedAction: Monitor for stronger stimulant effect. Carried forward from the uploaded record.
interactions.note: Raised gastric pH increases absorption of amphetamine, a weak base. Cimetidine's urinary alkalinising tendency additionally reduces renal excretion — the larger of the two effects.

interactions.note: Raised gastric pH plus reduced renal clearance, as for the IR form.

interactions.suggestedAction: No action needed; the direction of this one is protective.
interactions.note: Recorded so the pair is not left looking unexamined. Acid suppression reduces aspirin-related mucosal injury.

interactionScreening.note: Clean at therapeutic doses. Cimetidine's CYP inhibition includes weak CYP2E1 effects, which would if anything be mildly protective against NAPQI formation, but this is not a basis for any clinical action.

notes: The most interaction-prone drug in this set, and the reason it is worth pairing against famotidine in the same database: they do the same clinical job and have completely different interaction profiles. Every major cimetidine interaction below is enzyme inhibition, not H2 blockade.
